test_name: Monthly on a date that some months lack
test_description: Months too short for the date are skipped rather than clamped
test_precondition: Signed in. Server clock pinned to a known instant
step_description: Create an alarm repeating monthly on day 31 and read its next twelve occurrences
step_expected_result: Occurrences fall only in months that have a 31st. February never produces one, and no occurrence is moved to the 28th or 30th

test_name: Monthly on the nth weekday
step_description: Create an alarm repeating on the second Tuesday of each month and read its next twelve occurrences
step_expected_result: Each occurrence is the second Tuesday of its month

test_name: Monthly on the nth weekday
step_description: Create an alarm repeating on the fifth Friday of each month
step_expected_result: Months with no fifth Friday are skipped entirely rather than falling back to the fourth

test_name: Last weekday of the month
step_description: Create an alarm repeating on the last Friday of each month
step_expected_result: Each occurrence is that month's final Friday, whether the month has four or five

test_name: Spring forward across a missing hour
test_description: A local time that does not exist on the day the clocks go forward
test_precondition: Signed in. Timezone with daylight saving. Server clock pinned
step_description: Create a daily alarm at 02:30 in a timezone whose clocks jump from 02:00 to 03:00 on a known date
step_expected_result: On that date the occurrence is 03:30 - moved forward by the length of the gap. Surrounding days remain at 02:30

test_name: Fall back across a repeated hour
test_description: A local time that happens twice on the day the clocks go back
test_precondition: Signed in. Timezone with daylight saving. Server clock pinned
step_description: Create a daily alarm at 01:30 in a timezone whose clocks repeat 01:00 to 02:00 on a known date
step_expected_result: On that date there is exactly one occurrence, at the first and earlier-offset 01:30, not two

test_name: Repeat within a day at second intervals
step_description: Create an alarm starting at 09:00 repeating every 30 seconds until 09:05
step_expected_result: Occurrences are produced every 30 seconds within the window and none outside it, giving eleven for that day

test_name: Repeat within a day at second intervals
step_description: Combine the same window with a weekly rule
step_expected_result: The window repeats only on the selected weekdays

test_name: End after a set number of occurrences
step_description: Create a daily alarm ending after five occurrences
step_expected_result: Exactly five occurrences are produced and the series then stops

test_name: A window too dense to schedule
step_description: Create an alarm whose window and interval would produce more than four thousand occurrences in one day
step_expected_result: Creation is refused, and the message states the ceiling and the longest window the chosen interval allows

test_name: A self-destructing alarm removes itself
test_precondition: Signed in. Server clock can be pinned
step_description: Create an alarm marked self-destructing whose only occurrence is already in the past
step_expected_result: The alarm is absent from the list it should have appeared in

test_name: A self-destructing alarm removes itself
test_precondition: Signed in. Server clock can be pinned
step_description: Create a self-destructing alarm with occurrences still ahead of it
step_expected_result: The alarm is present and is not removed while it still has something to fire

test_name: An alarm with no group is listed at the top level
step_description: Create an alarm without choosing a group
step_expected_result: The alarm appears on the groups page outside any group, not inside one called Unfiled

test_name: An alarm with no group is listed at the top level
step_description: Move it into a group and then back out again
step_expected_result: It moves into the group and returns to the top level

test_name: Alarm raises a notification with the right message
test_description: Split from the manual check so the automated half is a whole case
test_precondition: Signed in. Notification permission granted. Browser clock controllable
step_description: Create an alarm due shortly with a known spoken message and advance the browser clock past its moment
step_expected_result: A notification is raised carrying that alarm's name as its title and its note and local time in the body

test_name: Alarm raises a notification with the right message
test_description: Split from the manual check so the automated half is a whole case
test_precondition: Signed in. Notification permission granted. Browser clock controllable
step_description: Inspect what the application asked to be spoken
step_expected_result: The spoken text is the message configured on the alarm and the requested voice is the one chosen

test_name: Each repeat says something different
test_precondition: Signed in. Notification permission granted. Browser clock controllable
step_description: Create an alarm repeating within a day with an ordinary message and a closing message
step_expected_result: Earlier occurrences speak the ordinary message, and the final occurrence of the day speaks the closing one

test_name: Notification appears correctly on the desktop
test_description: The half of TC4 a browser cannot observe
test_precondition: Signed in on Windows with notifications allowed. An alarm due within a minute
step_description: Wait for the alarm to fire with the application open
step_expected_result: A Windows notification appears showing the alarm's name and its message, and the voice is audible and intelligible

test_name: Speech voices resolve on each engine
test_description: The real cross-browser risk - voices are supplied by the browser and the operating system
test_precondition: An alarm with a spoken message and a chosen voice
step_description: Open the alarm preview in Chromium then Firefox then WebKit and inspect which voice each resolves
step_expected_result: Each engine resolves some voice and none fails outright. Differences between engines are recorded rather than treated as failures

test_name: Date and time inputs are usable on each engine
test_description: Each engine renders these controls differently
step_description: Complete the schedule step on Chromium then Firefox then WebKit
step_expected_result: The time and start date can be set on every engine and the values are retained, whatever the picker looks like

test_name: The timezone list is populated on each engine
test_description: The list is built from the browser's own timezone data
step_description: Open the timezone field on each engine
step_expected_result: A non-empty list of IANA names is offered and the application's default is among them

test_name: The layout works at phone width
step_description: View the groups page and the create wizard at 390 pixels wide
step_expected_result: No horizontal scrolling, no overlapping controls, and every action remains reachable

test_name: Deleting a group deletes its alarms
test_description: The assertion the API cannot make on its own
test_precondition: Signed in. A group containing at least two alarms. Direct database access
step_description: Delete the group with confirmation
step_expected_result: The group is gone from the list

test_name: Deleting a group deletes its alarms
test_description: The assertion the API cannot make on its own
test_precondition: Signed in. A group containing at least two alarms. Direct database access
step_description: Query the database for alarms that referenced that group
step_expected_result: No rows remain. The alarms were deleted rather than orphaned with a dangling reference

test_name: Deleting an account removes everything it owned
test_precondition: An account with groups and alarms. Direct database access
step_description: Delete the account
step_expected_result: The account can no longer sign in

test_name: Deleting an account removes everything it owned
test_precondition: An account with groups and alarms. Direct database access
step_description: Query the database for that user's groups and alarms
step_expected_result: No rows remain for that user in either table

test_name: Deleting an alarm leaves its group intact
test_precondition: Signed in with a group holding two alarms
step_description: Delete one alarm from the group
step_expected_result: The alarm is gone and the group remains with its other alarm

test_name: A write without the CSRF token is refused
test_precondition: Signed in with a valid session
step_description: Send a create-alarm request carrying the session cookie but no x-csrf-token header
step_expected_result: The request is refused and no alarm is created

test_name: A write without the CSRF token is refused
test_precondition: Signed in with a valid session
step_description: Send the same request with an incorrect token
step_expected_result: The request is refused in the same way

test_name: Passwords are stored as hashes
test_precondition: An account exists. Direct database access
step_description: Read the stored credential for a known account
step_expected_result: The value is a scrypt hash with its parameters and salt. The password does not appear anywhere in it, in any encoding

test_name: A password reset ends every other session
test_precondition: An account signed in from two separate clients
step_description: Complete a password reset using one client
step_expected_result: That client is signed in with the new password

test_name: A password reset ends every other session
test_precondition: An account signed in from two separate clients
step_description: Make a request from the second client using its existing session
step_expected_result: The session is rejected. A reset ends every session the account had

test_name: Input that looks like code is stored and shown as text
step_description: Create an alarm whose name contains a single quote and a semicolon
step_expected_result: The alarm is created with that exact name, and no database error occurs

test_name: Input that looks like code is stored and shown as text
step_description: Create an alarm whose name contains a script tag and view the list
step_expected_result: The name is displayed as literal text and nothing is executed

test_name: Alarm name length limits
step_description: Create alarms with names of 1 and 80 characters
step_expected_result: Both are accepted

test_name: Alarm name length limits
step_description: Create alarms with names of 0 and 81 characters
step_expected_result: Both are refused with a field error on the name

test_name: Interval range limits
step_description: Create interval alarms with every set to 1 and to 365
step_expected_result: Both are accepted

test_name: Interval range limits
step_description: Create interval alarms with every set to 0 and to 366
step_expected_result: Both are refused with a field error

test_name: Occurrence count limits
step_description: Create alarms ending after 1 and after 1000 occurrences
step_expected_result: Both are accepted

test_name: Occurrence count limits
step_description: Create alarms ending after 0 and after 1001 occurrences
step_expected_result: Both are refused with a field error

test_name: Spoken message length limit
step_description: Create an alarm with a spoken message of exactly 200 characters
step_expected_result: It is accepted

test_name: Spoken message length limit
step_description: Create an alarm with a spoken message of 201 characters
step_expected_result: It is refused with a field error on the message
